name: Craft
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Write visually polished documents, link them, and export a portable personal library

pricing.notes: Typical Plus monthly price; regional App Store amounts can vary.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1,500 content blocks; 1 GB storage; 25 MB/file; 7-day version history; 15 AI credits

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Unlimited documents; 5 spaces; 1 TB/space; 5 GB/file; 30-day history; 50 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Family
tiers.limits: 2–6 accounts total; 5 shared family spaces; each member gets Plus and 5 personal 1 TB spaces
tiers.notes: Annual total is $180; invite up to 5 other members.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Up to 10 members; 25 shared team spaces; every member gets Plus and 5 personal 1 TB spaces

tiers.name: Education
tiers.limits: Eligible students/educators: unlimited documents; 5 spaces; 250 GB total; 1 GB/file; 15 lifetime AI credits

tiers.name: Larger teams
tiers.limits: More than 10 members; custom seat/space terms

pricing.freeTierCaps: Starter: 1,500 blocks, 1 GB storage, 25 MB/file, 7-day history and 15 AI credits
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; direct subscriptions have a 14-day refund window; App Store/Setapp terms differ
pricing.hiddenCosts: Family and Team are flat bundles with hard member ceilings (6 and 10 total). AI is credit-limited even on paid plans. Education requires yearly re-verification; larger teams need a quote.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Craft, write visually polished documents, link them, and export a portable personal library. The hard boundary is native apps, sync, publishing, collaboration, and strong block-editor polish, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Write visually polished documents as linked notes, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export the personal library as a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: native apps, sync, publishing, collaboration, and strong block-editor polish
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Craft because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Polished documents, links and canvases, with local workspaces and usable exports.

facts.install: Use AFFiNE Cloud or install the desktop app; self-hosted collaboration uses the official Docker Compose stack with AFFiNE, PostgreSQL, and Redis
facts.engines: AFFiNE AI supports bring-your-own-key routes for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and FAL; local storage is available in the desktop app, while self-host AI is configured server-side
facts.dataFormat: A local-only desktop workspace stays on that device; AFFiNE Cloud stores it in AFFiNE's service, while self-hosted workspaces use PostgreSQL for structured data, mounted blob storage for uploads, Redis for cache, and local configuration files
facts.gapVsPaid: It approaches Craft's documents and canvases, but typography, sharing, publishing, export consistency, and collaborative polish are less mature.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app is straightforward, but free self-hosted sync and collaboration require Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, persistent volumes, configuration, migrations, backups, and a correctly exposed server URL

alternatives.name: AppFlowy
alternatives.desc: A portable document workspace that trades Craft's sheen for local control.

facts.install: Install a native desktop/mobile app or use AppFlowy Web/Cloud; self-hosting deploys the AppFlowy Cloud Docker stack and points the clients at it
facts.engines: Hosted plans expose managed models such as GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet; local/on-prem use can connect Ollama, LM Studio, or another self-hosted LLM
facts.dataFormat: Offline work remains in the device's local AppFlowy store; AppFlowy Cloud syncs it to AppFlowy's service, while the self-hosted stack persists workspace/auth data in PostgreSQL, cache/queues in Redis, and uploads in MinIO or another S3-compatible object store
facts.gapVsPaid: It provides local control and structured documents, but Craft's visual layouts, presentation quality, publishing, and collaboration remain more polished.
facts.setupBlocker: Local offline use installs cleanly, but self-hosted sync is a multi-container deployment with PostgreSQL, Redis, GoTrue authentication, object storage, mail/auth secrets, migrations, and client URL configuration

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.desc: Linked documents in ordinary Markdown; beautiful publishing is your own department.

facts.install: Install the native Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, or Android app; no account is required for local use
facts.dataFormat: Ordinary Markdown files and attachments in a user-chosen local vault folder, with app settings and plugins under `.obsidian`; optional paid Obsidian Sync stores end-to-end-encrypted replicas in Obsidian's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It makes a wonderfully portable linked library, but it lacks Craft's visual block layouts, effortless beautiful documents, and integrated publishing experience.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Craft in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: write visually polished documents as linked notes, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export the personal library as a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
